evidence.excerpt:
Implant placement in the posterior edentulous maxilla is clinically challenging due to anatomical variability, 
limited residual bone height, and maxillary sinus pneumatization. Conventional planning relies heavily on 
clinician experience and manual radiographic interpretation, leading to variability and subjectivity. This study 
developed and evaluated a two-stage Vision Transformer (ViT)–based deep learning framework for multi-
output classification of implant placement parameters from cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) images. 
A retrospective dataset of 457 expert-validated posterior maxillary edentulous cases was collected from the 
Faculty of Dentistry, Mahidol University. The model simultaneously classified four planning parameters—
implant height, implant diameter, sinus lift technique, and sinus lift stage—using a multi-output architecture 
with task-specific classification

Dataset partitioning
The final dataset of 457 images was divided into training, validation, and test sets comprising 367 (80.3%), 45

All CBCT cross-sectional images were preprocessed through a standardized image-processing pipeline to ensure 
consistency and optimize feature extraction for deep learning analysis. Each exported CBCT image (1920 × 1080 
pixels, JPEG format) was first converted into a two-dimensional format and normalized for intensity consistency.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: The experimental results support the headline claims that the ViT model outperforms standard CNN baselines (which collapsed to majority class predictions on implant height) and achieves an overall accuracy of 85.56% across the four tasks.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The framework is tested on a held-out test partition of 45 cases using standard classification metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC), attention rollout maps for anatomical interpretability, and latency benchmarking on CPU and GPU.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Standard supervised learning benchmark evaluated on a held-out dataset without model-in-the-loop evaluator reuse.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Held-out test set evaluation (n = 45) comparing model predictions against expert-consensus labels using classification accuracy, precision, recall, F1, and ROC-AUC.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised cross-entropy loss with label smoothing calculated against expert-consensus annotations on the training split.

primary.limitations: The authors transparently report key constraints including single-center retrospective data collection, reliance on 2D cross-sectional projections rather than 3D volumetric data, a modest test set size (n = 45), class imbalances affecting minority classes, and reliance on expert consensus rather than longitudinal clinical outcomes.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, covering ethical approval, 2D composite quadrant preprocessing from 3D Accuitomo CBCT images, an expert panel annotation process with majority-vote consensus, a two-stage training scheme (frozen backbone stage followed by end-to-end fine-tuning), and comparison against four standard CNN backbones.
primary.quality_rationale: The study provides a substantive technical and clinical contribution with a clear pipeline, appropriate baseline comparisons, sound interpretability analysis, and careful qualification of limitations.
primary.scoped_contribution: The manuscript presents a two-stage fine-tuning Vision Transformer (ViT) framework for multi-output classification of four dental implant placement parameters (implant height, implant diameter, sinus lift technique, and sinus lift stage) from CBCT cross-sectional composite images.
